agent-pipeline run <runId> · <duration>

  merged   #3 Run: drain the Frontier (PR #12)
  noted    #8 comment · from #3 implement · the CLI help drifts from the README
  handed   #5 Fix Stage with a single retry · verify · 1 unmet
  noted    #31 new · from #5 fix · nothing cleans up abandoned worktrees
  skipped  #7 no-criteria
  skipped  #9 blocked

Frontier empty.

The verb is padded to nine columns so the Ticket numbers line up. A Run that
took no Ticket prints `  nothing to do` in place of the rows.

`released` is a Ticket the subscription rate limit stopped mid-flight: its Claim
was undone, and the State file it has been keeping since it was claimed says
where the next Run resumes it from. Nobody has to do anything about it, which is
why it is not `handed`. It is the last row of its Run, which ends there:

agent-pipeline run <runId> · <duration>

  merged   #3 Run: drain the Frontier (PR #12)
  released #6 Rebase conflict resolution · rate limit at implement

Rate limited.

A Ticket a Run resumed has no row of its own, released or stranded: it merges,
is handed off, or is released again like any other, and the header already names
the Run that took it.

`skipped` names why a candidate was passed over: `blocked` for one an open
blocker held back all Run, and otherwise the guard reason that kept it from
being claimed — `spec`, `no-criteria` or `body-only-blockers` for Planning a
guard rejected, `claimed` or `not-ready` for an issue that is nobody's to take,
which is usually one `ticket <n>` named by hand. A stranded Ticket is not one of
those: it wears this checkout's own Claim, so it is resumed rather than `skipped`
as `claimed`.

`noted` is a Note a Stage made, and follows the row of the Ticket whose Stage
made it. Its number is where the Note went, not where it came from: `comment`
for a Note posted on the Ticket it named, `new` for one that named none and got
a `needs-triage` issue of its own. The note itself is trimmed to one line; the
whole of it is on GitHub.

The last line says why the Run stopped: `Frontier empty.` when nothing is left,
`Frontier blocked.` when every remaining candidate has an open blocker, and
`Rate limited.` when a Release ended the Run.

A Run the limit stopped prints no `skipped  #<n> blocked` rows and no rows for
the Frontier Tickets it never reached: it stopped before it could say a
candidate was held back all Run. The `released` row and the last line are the
whole report.

`ticket <n>` prints the same header and its one row, and stops there: it drains
no Frontier, so it says nothing about one.
